title: From Preferences to Principles: Rubric-Based Alignment for Grounded Knowledge Answers
gist: Apple researchers introduce a rubric-based reward framework for open-domain QA post-training that generates query-specific, evidence-grounded, multi-dimensional rubrics, beating an instruction-tuned baseline by 6.5% and flat-rubric variants by 4% across composition, grounding, and instruction-following metrics.

themes.theme: Rubric-based reward design for LLM post-training

insights.claim: Designing effective reward signals for open-domain question answering is hard because high-quality answers must simultaneously satisfy multiple distinct quality aspects that a single holistic scalar reward cannot capture.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Frames scalar reward models (a common RLHF default) as structurally inadequate for knowledge-grounded QA, a critique applicable to any team post-training assistants on factual Q&A tasks.
insights.quote: high-quality responses must simultaneously satisfy multiple aspects of answer quality that are difficult to capture with a holistic scalar objective
insights.locator: Designing effective reward signals for open-domain question answering

insights.claim: The proposed rubric-based reward framework generates query-specific rubrics grounded in retrieved evidence and decomposed into multiple quality dimensions, giving fine-grained supervision signals during LLM post-training.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A generalizable recipe (per-query rubric generation grounded in retrieved evidence) that other labs could adopt to replace flat reward models in QA and knowledge-assistant post-training.
insights.locator: We introduce a rubric-based reward framework

insights.claim: Averaged across three evaluation axes (composition, grounding, and instruction-following), the rubric-based approach improved over an instruction-tuned baseline by 6.5% and over flat (non-decomposed) rubric variants by 4%, with consistent gains across all evaluation datasets.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: A concrete, benchmarked improvement over both a plain instruction-tuned baseline and a simpler rubric ablation gives investors a quantifiable signal of how much reward-design sophistication is worth in QA quality.
insights.quote: our approach improves over the instruction-tuned baseline by 6.5% and over flat rubric variants by 4%, with consistent gains across all evaluation datasets

insights.claim: Conditioning rubrics on retrieved evidence specifically improves factual support/grounding of answers, while decomposing rubrics into separate quality-specific dimensions further improves coherence, organization, and adherence to query requirements.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Separates which design choice buys which benefit — evidence-grounding fixes factuality, decomposition fixes structure — useful for teams deciding which piece to adopt first if resource-constrained.
insights.quote: Conditioning rubrics on retrieved evidence improves factual support, while decomposing rubrics into quality-specific dimensions further improves coherence, organization, and adherence to query requirements.

insights.claim: A 2020 related Apple-linked dataset effort, MKQA (Multilingual Knowledge Questions and Answers), built an open-domain QA evaluation set of 10,000 question-answer pairs aligned across 26 typologically diverse languages, 260,000 QA pairs in total, to support cross-lingual model evaluation.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Shows a multi-year institutional research lineage in open-domain QA evaluation infrastructure at Apple, from multilingual benchmarks to today's rubric-based reward work.
insights.quote: Multilingual Knowledge Questions and Answers (MKQA), an open-domain question answering evaluation set comprising 10k question-answer pairs aligned across 26 typologically diverse languages (260k question-answer pairs in total)
